groups.passage:
Authors write for many reasons. Often they write about real or make-believe people, places, or events that may be funny, sad, or scary. Sometimes authors write about these things to entertain readers. Authors also write about these things to inform by giving facts or ideas.
The following two paragraphs are examples of these two kinds.
(1) When he finished with unpacking, Nelson carried all the empty boxes down the hallway. On his way to the dump, the bell rang. He needed to hurry. He had no time to go to the dump. Then, he stopped at Adam Joshua’s office, which happened to be unlocked, and walked away joyfully. Later in the afternoon, Nelson came to Adam’s office with Peter for their biology project. The empty boxes and many other things fell all over them the minute he opened the door. “Adam Joshua!” yelled Nelson, pushing away a basketball and shaking a toy frog off his foot. “This is no way to treat a friend!”
(2) Where the land meets the sea we find seashells. There are many different kinds of shells. They can be round like the moon, long like a jackknife, or shaped like boxes, fans, or tops. The shells we find are usually empty, but once there were soft bodies inside. Animals with hard shells outside and soft bodies inside are called mollusks.

groups.passage:
Kauai, the oldest of the main Hawaiian Islands, has some of the state’s most stunning scenery. Rivers and streams flow slowly through jungles of shaded greens. The breathtaking 4,000-foot cliffs of Na Pali Coast rise grandly from the sea. Waimea Canyon, called the "Grand Canyon of the Pacific" by Mark Twain, cuts a deep gash through the rugged central mountains.
Rising more than 5,000 feet, Mt. Waialeale stands at the center of the nearly round island. This extinct volcano is considered the wettest spot on earth, with almost 500 inches of rainfall each year. Yet this amount of rain is surprisingly localized. Just a few miles west, there’s a dry region that receives a mere 6 inches of rain annually.
The island continues to recover from its 1992 visit from Iniki, the most powerful hurricane to hit Hawaii this century. A few hotels are still being rebuilt, but Kauai remains as beautiful as ever.
Kauai is not for people who thrive on crowds or nightlife. While it does have its share of resort hotels, shopping centers and good restaurants, and a smattering of museums, art galleries and night spots, its main attractions lie outdoors. Hiking, camping, and scuba diving are excellent on the island.

groups.passage: All living things die eventually. In ecological terms, the chemicals of living things are borrowed from the Earth, and at death they return. All the material that every animal, from the smallest fly to the largest elephant, takes in as food also returns to the Earth, as waste matter. The dead material and waste matter form the diet of a group of living organisms called decomposers. They include a range of bacteria, fungi, and small animals that break down nature’s wastes into ever smaller pieces until all the chemicals are released into the air, the soil, and the water, making them available to other living things. Without the carbon dioxide released from the process, all plant life would die out. Without the oxygen that plants give out, and without the food that they supply, life would grind to a halt and all animals would starve. The decomposers are a vital link in the natural cycle of life and death.

groups.passage:
New York, Nov. 17--In a swirl of confetti and shredded paper, John Glenn made his second trip through New York’s "Canyon of Heroes" in a parade Monday, saluting his return to space 36 years after he became America’s first man in orbit.
Glenn’s first ticker-tape parade on March 1, 1962, after his Mercury flight, is considered the largest ever in New York. An estimated 3,474 tons of confetti and ticker-tape rained down along a seven-mile route.
For his second parade, despite lunchtime crowds from Wall Street, the turnout Monday was sparse by New York standards and spectators along a route less than a mile long were surprisingly restrained. Police and Glenn’s parade was attended by 500,000 -- a figure that appeared generously inflated.
The 1962 celebration "was more enthusiastic -- a lot more people," said one spectator, who as a young newlywed attended Glenn’s first parade and came from her Brooklyn home again for Glenn’s second parade.
Another spectator said that too many Americans take the achievements of the space program for granted. "It’s become so everyday, so ordinary, nobody cares," he said.
Glenn began the day with decorating the Rockefeller Center Christmas tree. After that event, Glenn recalled the 1962 parade, saying, "It was just so enormous. I remember just a blizzard of paper. You could hardly even look up without getting something in your eye."
Glenn, who retires from the U.S. Senate next month, joins a list of individuals and sports teams honored with more than one ticker-tape parade.

options.B: became the first man to land on the moon.

options.B: The huge amount of paper poured over him.
options.C: The Christmas tree in front of the Rockefeller Center.
options.D: The key to the city he received from the mayor.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is TRUE?

options.A: John Glenn is admirable in that he has been to the moon more than once.
options.B: Only John Glenn has received the ticker-tape parade more than once.
options.C: Many Americans are no longer excited about space achievements.
options.D: Glenn’s second parade in New York was larger than the first one.

questions.stem: According to the passage, how many space flights has Glenn taken?
Why does the report say that the figure of Glenn’s second parade was “inflated”?

options.A: Because the second parade had a larger crowd than the first parade.
options.B: Because there were many people who attended both parades.
options.C: Because the crowd of the second parade seemed to be far less than 500,000.
options.D: Because the crowd of the second parade was far more enthusiastic.

sections.title: 二、英文作文（20%）
sections.instructions:
說明：1.請依提示在「答案卷」上寫一篇英文作文。
2.文長約120字。

questions.label: 英文作文
questions.stem: 根據以上四則求職廣告，寫一篇英文作文。文分兩段：第一段寫出你認為這四種工作中那一種對你而言是最好的工作，並說明理由；第二段則寫出四種工作中你最不可能選擇的工作，也說明理由。假如這四種工作你都不喜歡，則在第一段說明都不喜歡的理由，在第二段寫你喜歡什麼工作，並說明理由。

tags.topic: which of the four advertised jobs is best for you and which you would be least likely to choose, with reasons (or, if none appeals, why, and what job you like)
choosing a job from job advertisements

extraction.method: 官方 Word 版（paper-2.doc → soffice 轉 docx → python-docx，含求職廣告所在的表格）取文字，與 pdftotext -layout 逐段比對，並以 Read 逐頁檢視題本 PDF 影像（8 頁）確認版面、空格位置、段落與廣告格式；答案檔為多科合併的掃描檔，以 Read 看影像並以 150dpi 裁切英文欄放大逐題抄錄。
issues: 無統計資料：units.json 中 88 學年度只有題本（PDF、Word）與選擇題答案，沒有 stats（答對率／鑑別度／選項分析）與 scoring 檔，所有小題 stats 為 null，sources.scoring／stats 為空陣列（validator 的「整份考卷沒有任何統計資料」warning 屬實）。
答案檔（answer.pdf）為國文、英文、數學合併的掃描影像（第1頁「八十八學年學科能力測驗國文考科、英文考科及數學考科答案」，第2頁為社會、自然），以 Read 看影像並以 150dpi 裁切英文欄放大逐題抄錄第1–55題；每題答案皆與題意核對過一致。
簡答題第1–5題：大考中心未公布簡答題參考答案或評分原則（答案檔只有選擇題），answer／accepted_answers／scoring_notes 均填 null。英文作文亦無官方評分原則，answer 為 null。

第16–20題：題本將一段旅館櫃台對話克漏字放在「一、詞彙與語法（20%）」大題內（16-20題為題組），各題只有選項、沒有題幹。為維持題本大題結構（第1–20題同一大題、20分），放在 vocabulary 大題的第二個題組 s1g2，對話原文放 passage 並以 [[16]]–[[20]] 標空格；validator 規定 vocabulary 單選題必須有 stem，因此 stem 填入該空格所在的那一句（不含說話者，空格改為 ______），這是從選文複製的原句，不是題本另外印的題幹（與 gsat-89 作法一致）。
非選擇題題號：簡答題題本印為 1.–5.，與選擇題第1–5題重號，因此 no 保留 1–5、label 改為「簡答1」–「簡答5」；英文作文題本未編號，no 填 1、label 為「作文」。validator 的「題號重複 [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]」warning 因此產生，屬合理。

結構與 gsat-spec.json legacy_gsat 88–89 期別一致：詞彙與語法 1–20（每題1分，20分）、綜合測驗 21–40（每題1分，20分）、閱讀測驗 41–55（每題2分，30分）、簡答題 5題×2分（10分）、英文作文 20分（文長約120字）；合計 100 分。題本封面：考試時間100分鐘、單一選擇題共55題（1~55題）、非選擇題共兩大題。第一部分標題原文為「第一部分：單一選擇題」，part 填「單一選擇題」；簡答題標題題本只印「一、簡答題」（未標百分比），配分取自說明「每題2分，共10分」。

簡答題的四則求職廣告（題本第7頁，2×2 方框）以 passage_parts 的 A–D 記錄全文；A、C、D 以各框置中加框／加灰底的標題為 title，B 的醒目職稱「Service Technician」是首句「An international company requires a」的一部分，故 B 的 title 為 null、全文依原順序放 text（保留換行）。版面格式（粗體、斜體、灰底、加框）不保留，另以 figures 中 kind=advertisement 的說明文字描述。A 末句「please call 2742-6996」題本無句點，照原樣保留；C 的列點符號在 PDF 與 Word 版都是「﹪」(U+FE6A)，照原樣保留；C 末兩行「Fax resume and work samples, if any, to / The China Post at (03) 2595-7962.」是同一句，合併為一行；D 的「OPENINGS」後接 29 個星號（依 Word 版計數）。
英文作文的提示引用簡答題的「以上四則求職廣告」（s4g1 passage_parts），作文題組本身沒有附圖或選文。作文 essay_type 標為 two_paragraph（提示要求「文分兩段」）。
說明文字的換行：Word 版用手動段落換行排版（如「注意答案要寫在「答案卷」」與「上。」分屬兩段、「題1與題5的答案用各則廣告的英文字母代號。」與「題2,3,4要寫job的名稱。…」分屬兩段），PDF 影像顯示為同一條說明的折行，因此同一編號說明內合併為一行，編號說明之間以 \n 分隔。簡答題第1、5題括號內的作答提示在題本另起一行，stem 中以 \n 分隔。

空格與空白：詞彙題空格在題本為底線，一律寫成 ______ 並前後各留一個空格（第2題 PDF 為「Wang ______changes」、第12題為「can______during」，底線緊貼後一字，屬排版，已正規化）；句間兩個空白一律改為一個。第16–20題對話中「(19) should be four more.」在 Word 版另起一段，但 PDF 影像顯示為 Guest 發言的懸掛縮排續行，因此併入同一行發言。
第21–30題選文在 Word 版於「they have」後斷成兩段，但 PDF 影像為同一段，passage 依 PDF 作一段。
格式：第42題與第48題題幹的 FALSE、第43題的 TRUE、第49題的 NOT、簡答第1題的 NOT 在題本為粗體；依規則不保留格式。

逐字保留題本原文，包括可疑之處：第51–55題選文「Police and Glenn’s parade was attended by 500,000」語意不通（原新聞應為「Police said Glenn’s parade…」之類），照題本保留；第41題選項 (A)「What’s a Friend for」無問號；第42題題本 Word 版題幹末有多餘空白已去除。引號依題本：第31–40、45–48、51–55題選文用直引號 "…"（撇號為彎引號 ’），第41–44題選文與第55題題幹用彎引號 “…”，照原樣保留。
